subject: GimmeSomeSlack

waived.scope: I don't much care about savegame continuity

advisory: Each of the four looks is judged by his eye; none is reject-level on its own (OWNER:1793590546413059482)

leaves.oracle_proposed: conduit Graphic alpha 0 on PowerConduit and WaterproofConduit; cord meshes present per edge; HiddenConduit cells own no cord edge; overlay connector count unchanged; captures at play zoom
leaves.tier_reason: drawing and the def's graphic are only real in a running game; a dev quicktest colony on the minimal list shows them in about 90 s
leaves.experience: The player, at play zoom over a powered room in each of the four looks, sees no vanilla conduit pipe anywhere: only loose cords show where power goes, while the power overlay still draws its connector lines. It must not read as vanilla conduit reskinned, or as a run with neither pipe nor cord. This holds for WaterproofConduit as for plain conduit.
leaves.scenario: Lay a conduit run with a battery, a generator and two consumers in each look; capture at play zoom with the overlay off and on; then lay a vanilla HiddenConduit run beside it. Include a WaterproofConduit run laid on shallow water beside the plain run.
false_pass: the conduit def's graphic swapped for a cord texture laid on the conduit cell, so a pipe-shaped cord follows the grid exactly
the conduit hidden and no cord drawn, so the room reads clean because nothing is drawn
leaves.red: conduit cells still draw the vanilla pipe under the cords, or a hidden-conduit run grows cords it should not
leaves.owner_part: yes: a room with no conduit pipe, only cords

leaves.oracle_proposed: per edge: drawn length / chord at least 1.4; no bend tighter than the minimum radius; at least one excursion of a cell or more off the conduit line per edge longer than four cells; captures
leaves.tier_reason: cord geometry is built in game from the live grid; a quicktest colony gives it in 90 s
leaves.experience: The player, at play zoom over a workshop floor of a dozen devices, sees every cord between two nodes lying in broad loose loops and coils, visibly much longer than the straight line between its ends, resisting tight turns, wandering off the conduit line and back. It must not read as a taut straight cable, a cord tracing the conduit cell by cell, or a hairpin kink.
leaves.scenario: Stage a 12x12 workshop with conduit in an L, a T and a straight run; read every edge's drawn length against its chord and its minimum bend radius; capture at play zoom.
false_pass: a fixed wavy texture tiled along the conduit, so length is long but the cord still traces the grid
slack only on the edges the test happens to read
leaves.red: cords are drawn straight between nodes, or follow the conduit cell by cell
leaves.owner_part: yes: the floor reads as over-long extension cords

leaves.oracle_proposed: the bridge `bends` probe (CordShapeAudit.Bends) over every strand on the map, ends included: tally unforced == 0, where a turn tighter than 90 degrees within one cell is forced only when a wall, building, door or socket next to it leaves no other way (row M2c_no_sharp_bends); and on the same strands in each look the sc_cords_slack read (leaf cords_lie_slack): drawn length at least 1.4 times the chord and an excursion of a cell or more off the conduit line on edges over four cells, so a taut straight cord fails
leaves.tier_reason: cord geometry is built in game from the live grid; a quicktest colony gives it in 90 s
leaves.experience: The player, at play zoom over a workshop floor in each of the four looks, sees every cord curve slowly, the way a real cord avoids a sharp bend: no cord turns tighter than 90 degrees within one cell unless a wall, a building, a door or a socket beside it forces the turn, and that holds at the plug and junction ends too. It must not read as a cord kinked into a hairpin or a V on open floor, or as slack bought with tight wiggles.
leaves.scenario: Lay the core workshop scene (a battery, a generator, junctions, consumers and a wall stub) in each look, then read every cord's bends; repeat on the dense block and the mast foot, where leads are short and turns are most tempting.
false_pass: bends read only mid-cord, so a hairpin where the cord leaves a plug or a junction passes
a bend called forced because some building is on the map, not because one sits beside the bend
cords drawn straight between their ends, so nothing bends at all and the bar is met by a taut cord
leaves.red: an unforced turn sharper than 90 degrees in one cell on open floor, such as the 235 degree hook on the junction-battery lead (RIMMANDRAKE_UNBEND_GSS_LEAD_AT_JUNCTION_BATTERY_TWICE)
leaves.owner_part: yes: cords on open floor that curve gently and kink only where a wall, building or socket makes them

leaves.oracle_proposed: every sampled point of every cord curve lies on a walkable cell or on a wall-face stub; each wall crossing has a stub on both faces; each dive has two plates; captures
leaves.tier_reason: walkability and the drawn curves exist only in game; a quicktest colony gives both
leaves.experience: The player, at play zoom where conduit runs into and through walls and past a rock outcrop, sees each cord pile against the wall and end at the wall's face as if it goes in there, coming out on the other face; no cord is drawn across the top of a wall, rock or any other impassable cell, and an unroutable cord dives under a barrier with a plate on each side. It must not read as a cord painted over a wall top or clipping through rock.
leaves.scenario: Conduit through a wall, along a wall, round a rock outcrop and into a fully enclosed unroutable pocket; read every cord vertex against walkability; capture both faces of each wall.
false_pass: the cord simply stops a cell short of the wall, so nothing crosses it but nothing meets the face either
vertices checked only at cell centres while the curve between them crosses the wall
leaves.red: a cord is drawn across the top of a wall or through rock
leaves.owner_part: yes: cords pile against walls and end at the wall face

leaves.oracle_proposed: for every NodeType.Junction: exactly one JunctionPiece of the look's family; every arm's end within the piece's socket tolerance (CordAudit arm check, blob junctions included); Modern pieces are the PowerStrip art; captures
leaves.tier_reason: junction nodes and their posed pieces exist only in the live cord graph
leaves.experience: The player, at play zoom over every 3-way and 4-way conduit junction in a base, sees a joining piece there with every cord at that junction plugging into it: in the Modern look the long power strip (at a 3-way it takes two cords plus its own lead), in the Industrial look the junction box, in Scrapper and Futuristic their own connector. It must not read as a cord passing through the junction with nothing joining it, a strip with a cord stopping short of it, or the splitter box in the Modern look.
leaves.scenario: Build a grid holding ten 3-way and ten 4-way junctions in each look, some inside a dense block; count joining pieces and plugged cord ends per junction; capture each look.
false_pass: one strip per room rather than per junction
the strip drawn while the cords end at the junction cell centre beside it
leaves.red: a 3-way junction draws no joining piece, or the Modern look still draws the splitter box at junctions
leaves.owner_part: yes: cords plugging into a strip or connector at every junction

leaves.oracle_proposed: tangle-pile pieces present over the block; cord crossings per cell above the sparse room's; a judge agent's read of the capture against the parallel-lines reject picture
leaves.tier_reason: the pile is a live drawing; a quicktest capture shows it
leaves.experience: The player, at play zoom over a 6x6 block packed with conduit, sees one tangled heap of wires and power strips all swirled together. It must not read as tidy parallel lines, a grid of identical cords, or an empty square.
leaves.scenario: Fill a 6x6 block with conduit in the Modern look beside a sparse room; capture both; a judge agent compares them against the reject picture of parallel lines.
false_pass: the dense block drawn as many independent slack cords that happen to run parallel
leaves.red: a dense block draws as parallel tidy lines
leaves.owner_part: yes: a dense block reads as a tangle

leaves.oracle_proposed: a bridge read that dumps sampled cord curves per edge, and an offline script that prints the distance table
leaves.tier_reason: the curves exist only in the live cord graph
leaves.experience: The log reports, for a set of cord edges of equal length and orientation, how different their drawn shapes are from one another, as a number per pair.
leaves.scenario: Read every edge's sampled curve from the cord graph, normalise to its chord, and print the pairwise shape distance for edges in the same length class.
false_pass: the distance computed on the edge seeds rather than on the drawn curve
leaves.red: every edge of the same length draws the identical curve, and nothing can tell

leaves.oracle_proposed: every pair of same-class edges above a minimum shape distance (cord_shape_variation_probe); a judge agent predicting his read of the capture
leaves.tier_reason: same as its instrument: the curves are live
leaves.experience: The player, at play zoom over a room with many cord runs of the same length side by side, sees no repeated pattern: each cord takes its own loops and coils, like real messy cables strewn across the floor. It must not read as a stamped tile or a row of identical squiggles.
leaves.scenario: Lay eight parallel conduit runs of the same length in one room; read the shape distance table; capture at play zoom for his eye and a judge agent.
false_pass: variation only in colour while the curve is the same
leaves.red: cords of the same length draw the same curve, so a room shows a repeating stamp
leaves.owner_part: yes: no repeating pattern on the floor

leaves.oracle_proposed: for every drawn cord: both ends in one PowerNet; each device has exactly one cord end per power connection; no cord end on a pipe slot; the adjacent-feed pump case named; every cord reaching a building with a pipe port enters its footprint on a diagonal segment and ends under it (slideUnder on)
leaves.tier_reason: PowerNets and drawn cords both exist only in the running game
leaves.experience: The player, reading a base's power only from its cords (the conduit is invisible), is told the truth: every cord joins two things on one power net, every device on a net has a cord reaching it, no device shows a second phantom cable, and no plug goes into a pipe slot. The route may be circuitous. It must not read as a cord joining two separate grids, a device fed by adjacent conduit wearing a second disconnected cable, or a plug in a pipe port. Where a cord reaches a building that has a pipe or hose port, it approaches on a diagonal and slides underneath the building, never straight into the port.
leaves.scenario: Stage two separate nets side by side, one cell apart; a pump fed by adjacent conduit that does not pass under it; a device with both power and pipe ports; read every cord edge's two ends against PowerNet membership and port kind.
false_pass: the check reads the conduit graph instead of the drawn cords, so a drawn cross-net cord passes
the adjacent-feed pump left out of the test
the slide-under check run only on buildings without a pipe port, where a straight approach is never tempted into the port
leaves.red: a cord bridges two separate power nets, or the adjacent-fed pump draws a second disconnected cable

leaves.oracle_proposed: after the cut: no edge spans the gap; two terminal ends; each end flagged live exactly when its PowerNet has a powered source (generator output or stored battery energy), dead otherwise; with a second source on the far side both ends live; after switch-off, an end whose net lost its last source clears within 250 ticks; captures
leaves.tier_reason: destroying a cell and reading PowerNet state needs the running game
leaves.experience: The player, at normal zoom after a conduit cell in a powered line is destroyed, sees two loose ends and no cord across the gap. Each end sparks only if it still has a path to some power source: in a line fed from one side, the fed end sparks and the far end lies limp and dead; if the far side has its own generator or battery, both ends spark, and that is right. Switching a source off makes an end that loses its last source dead within a few seconds. It must not read as an unbroken cord, as an end cut off from all power that still sparks, or as an end that still has power drawn limp and dead.
leaves.scenario: A generator, a run of conduit and a lamp; destroy a middle cell; read both terminal ends' state; switch the generator off and wait one 250-tick poll; capture before and after. Second case: a battery on the far side too; cut; both ends read live; switch only the generator off; the near end reads dead, the far end stays live.
false_pass: the ends drawn but the live/dead state taken from which side is nearer the generator rather than from power
a line that was never powered reading dead, passing for the switched-off case
only the single-source line tested, so a far side with its own battery reads dead and nobody sees it
leaves.red: a cut leaves an end that has no path to any power source sparking, or an end that still has power drawn dead, or the cord still drawn across the gap
leaves.owner_part: yes: one cut, a sparking live end and a dead end

leaves.oracle_proposed: shock hediff or damage on the live-end hauler, the visitor, the unrelated constructor and the hauler crossing the live end of the unfinished run, and on the live-end hauler again with the aerial master off; with maxSparkingEnds set to 1 and two live ends, shock on the hauler crossing each; none on the constructor whose job (delivering steel to or building) targets the blueprint or frame joining this end; none on the dead-end hauler or on the hauler crossing a live cord cell at least two cells from the end; every path asserted to cross the cell it is meant to
leaves.tier_reason: pawn jobs, PowerNet state and shock damage are live behaviour
leaves.experience: The player, at normal zoom over a workshop floor where a conduit cell was destroyed, sees a colonist hauling over the sparking live end shocked, and a visitor crossing it shocked too; the constructor carrying steel to and then rebuilding THAT conduit cell is not; a constructor building some other conduit who crosses the sparking end is shocked; a hauler crossing the limp dead end, or the live cord a few cells back from its end, is not. The loose end of a run the player simply stopped laying bites the same way, and every live end bites however many ends are sparking on the map. Turning off the overhead-lines master leaves floor ends biting. It must not read as the whole cord biting, a dead end that bites, a fixer shocked at the job, or every constructor safe.
leaves.scenario: A powered floor run fed from one side through a workshop, a second unrelated conduit blueprint, and a second powered run the player stopped laying short of its device; destroy a middle cell of the first; order a hauler across the live end cell, another across a live cord cell two or more cells back from that end, another across the dead end cell, and another across the unfinished run's loose end; a visitor walks across the live end; one constructor delivers steel to and builds the blueprint for the destroyed cell; another builds the unrelated blueprint and is routed across the live end; repeat the live-end crossing with the aerial master off, and with maxSparkingEnds at 1 across both live ends.
false_pass: the exemption keyed on any construction job instead of the conduit that joins this end
shock applied along the whole cord, so the end cell passes but harmless cells bite
floor-end shock gated on the aerial master, so it works only while overhead lines are on
only ends left by a destroyed cell bite, so a run the player stopped laying lies live and harmless
the exemption covers only the building step, so the constructor carrying steel to the joining blueprint is shocked
shock keyed on the spark budget's drawn set, so a live end past maxSparkingEnds stops biting
leaves.red: a pawn crossing a live floor-cord end on another job is not shocked, the constructor rebuilding that cell is, or a dead end bites
leaves.owner_part: yes: one cut on the workshop floor, a hauler shocked at the live end, the rebuilder safe

leaves.oracle_proposed: SliceWindow max slice ms and frame time per action; the touched edge's drawing is current after the action
leaves.tier_reason: frame time is only real in a running game on his machine; the minimal list keeps other mods' cost out
leaves.experience: at most 20 ms per frame of cord rebuild on the main thread on Archmagi, his machine, when a wire is placed, cut, dug past or a mast falls in a base of 2000 conduit cells
leaves.scenario: A 2000-cell conduit base with masts; place a cell, cut one, dig beside one, kill a mast, each alone and then in a burst of ten; read the slice timer and frame time.
false_pass: the rebuild skipped (stale drawing) so the frame is cheap
only the burst case read, hiding the lone-rebuild cost
leaves.red: a lone rebuild on a large base takes 140 ms on the main thread

leaves.oracle_proposed: span altitude layer above pawns and buildings; sag depth above zero; the three bad links refused with their reasons; one PowerNet across every span, the lamp mast's included, and its lamp lit; captures
leaves.tier_reason: draw layers and link refusal live in the running game
leaves.experience: The player, at play zoom over a yard where a sagging line crosses from a mast to a far mast over a wall, a building and a walking colonist, sees the span drawn above all of them, sagging between its anchors. It must not read as a line passing under a pawn or a roof, or a ruler-straight wire.
leaves.scenario: Two masts, a lamp mast and a wall bracket linked across a shed and a walkway; a colonist walks under; out-of-range, hostile and non-anchor links attempted; capture.
false_pass: the span drawn above only because nothing stands under it in the capture
leaves.red: an overhead span draws under a pawn or a building, or an out-of-range link is accepted
leaves.owner_part: yes: a sagging line crossing to a far mast

leaves.oracle_proposed: fallen wire present at ground layer below pawns; live/dead ends per net state; captures
leaves.tier_reason: killing a mast and drawing the fallen wire needs the running game
leaves.experience: The player, after a mast is killed or a span is cut by an explosion, sees the wire lying on the ground below pawns, its live end sparking and its dead end limp. It must not read as a span still hanging in the air, or a wire that vanished.
leaves.scenario: A powered span between two masts; kill one mast; on a second span, explode a charge under it; read each fallen wire's layer and ends; capture.
false_pass: the span hidden on cut, so nothing hangs but nothing lies either
leaves.red: a cut span keeps hanging in the air between the masts
leaves.owner_part: yes: one wire lying sparking on the ground

leaves.oracle_proposed: shock hediff or damage on the hauler, the visitor and the colonist re-stringing the OTHER span; none on the colonist whose RM_RestringSpan job targets this wire; none on the dead-wire haul; every exempt and every shocked path is asserted to cross the sparking end
leaves.tier_reason: pawn jobs and shock damage are live behaviour
leaves.experience: The player sees a colonist hauling across a live fallen wire get shocked, and a visitor crossing it shocked too, while the colonist who walks up to re-string THAT wire is not; a colonist on a re-string job for a different span who crosses this sparking end is shocked like anyone else; a dead fallen wire shocks no one. It must not read as shocks from thin air, a fixer shocked at the job, anyone on any re-string job walking through live wire unharmed, or a dead wire that still bites.
leaves.scenario: A live fallen wire across a hauling path, and a second cut span elsewhere; one colonist hauls across the live wire; a visitor walks across; a second colonist takes the re-string job for this wire; a third takes the re-string job for the other span and is routed across this wire's sparking end; then cut power and repeat the haul.
false_pass: the fixer exempt because no pawn ever steps on the sparking cell during the test
every pawn exempt, so no one is shocked and the fixer passes
the exemption keyed on the job type (anyone on RM_RestringSpan is safe) instead of on the wire the job targets
leaves.red: the colonist re-stringing the wire is shocked, a colonist re-stringing a different span walks through this live wire unharmed, or no one crossing a live wire is

leaves.oracle_proposed: default reads All; per value, shock on the floor-end crossing exactly under All, and on the downed-wire crossing and the FlowWorks collapsed-deck cord crossing under All and Only downed lines; no shock under None; no restart between values
leaves.tier_reason: the setting's effect is shock damage on live pawns
leaves.experience: The player opens Mod Settings and finds one shock choice with three values, None, Only downed lines and All, set to All on a fresh install. Under All a hauler crossing a live floor end, one crossing a live fallen wire and one crossing the live power cord a collapsed FlowWorks bridge deck dropped are all shocked; under Only downed lines the fallen wire and the dropped deck cord bite and the floor end does not; under None nothing does; the change takes effect without a restart. It must not read as an on/off box, a default other than All, or a choice that needs a restart.
leaves.scenario: A live floor-cord end, a live fallen wire and a FlowWorks bridge deck collapsed with a powered cord on it, on one map; for each of the three values, a hauler crosses each; read the default on a fresh settings file.
false_pass: the old on/off fallenWireShock kept and the third value wired to it, so Only downed lines and All behave alike
Only downed lines reads only GSS's own aerial strands, so FlowWorks' dropped deck cords fall silent or None leaves them biting
leaves.red: Only downed lines still shocks at a floor end, None still shocks, or the default is not All

leaves.oracle_proposed: alert lists both the cut anchor and the grounded one; its jump puts the camera on the listed anchor; a pawn's job is RM_RestringSpan at that anchor; after it, the span exists, one PowerNet spans it, and the alert drops that anchor; the toggle hides it
leaves.tier_reason: the job and the alert are live
leaves.experience: The player sees a Wire down alert listing the cut anchor, jumps to it, and a colonist goes there on a re-string job and strings the span back up; power flows again and the alert clears. It must not read as a span that heals itself with no colonist, or an alert that stays after the fix.
leaves.scenario: Cut a powered span; kill a second span's mast so its wire is grounded; read the alert; jump to each listed anchor; let a colonist take RM_RestringSpan; read the span, the net and the alert after; toggle the alert setting off and confirm it hides.
false_pass: the span restored by the test calling the link directly
leaves.red: a cut span never gets a re-string job, or comes back with no colonist doing it

leaves.oracle_proposed: a fire on the puddle cell within the poll window with fallenWireIgnites on and the wire live; none with the switch off; none with the wire dead; none on a chemfuel puddle under a live floor-cord end with shock reach All and the switch on
leaves.tier_reason: fire and filth are live state
leaves.experience: The player sees spilled fuel lying under the sparking end of a live fallen wire catch fire; under a dead wire it does not, and fuel under the sparking end of a cut floor cord does not either. It must not read as fuel that a live fallen wire never lights, or a fire that starts with no fallen wire there.
leaves.scenario: A live fallen wire with a chemfuel puddle on its sparking-end cell; wait; then the same with fallenWireIgnites off, and with the wire's source switched off. Then a chemfuel puddle on the live end cell of a cut floor cord, switch on, shock reach All.
false_pass: the fire comes from something else on the cell (heat, a lamp, a burning pawn), so a wire that never ignites passes
the ignition sweep widened to floor ends along with shock, so a cut floor cord lights fuel
leaves.red: a fuel puddle under a live sparking end never catches fire, or a dead wire lights it

leaves.oracle_proposed: tap net draws from the victim's net only; goodwill of the victim faction falls each day after sighting and stops after removal; no drain without a witness; every other faction's goodwill unchanged across the same window
leaves.tier_reason: factions, goodwill and sight are live
leaves.experience: The player clamps a power tap onto a neighbour's line and sees their power flow one way into the colony; when a pawn of theirs sees the clamp, goodwill with them drains steadily, and removing the clamp stops it. It must not read as free power with no risk, a one-off goodwill hit, or the drain hitting the wrong faction.
leaves.scenario: A neighbour settlement's powered line on the map; clamp a tap; read power flow; walk one of their pawns into sight; read goodwill over two days; remove the clamp; read again. Control: the clamp with no witness.
false_pass: the goodwill change from another cause (a gift, a raid) in the same window
power read flowing both ways
only the victim's goodwill is read, so a drain that also hits a third faction passes
leaves.red: a caught tap costs no goodwill, or costs a different faction

leaves.oracle_proposed: each run's members report one style; the merged run reports one; captures judged against the four reference sheets
leaves.tier_reason: style picks and drawing are live
leaves.experience: The player, at play zoom over four separate runs built in Scrapper, Industrial, Modern and Futuristic, tells each look apart by its cords, poles and connectors; every piece of one connected run draws in one look, its lamps included, while two runs side by side differ. It must not read as one look recoloured, or a run that changes look midway.
leaves.scenario: Four runs side by side, one per look, each with a mast and a lamp; join two of them and read the merged run's look; capture.
false_pass: the looks differing only by tint
leaves.red: one connected run draws in two looks, or two looks are indistinguishable

leaves.oracle_proposed: per switch: the feature's observable state differs between off and on and returns on flip-back; master off: conduit draws vanilla AND a lamp on a styled run draws its vanilla lamp graphic, both without a restart, and both return on master on; a read of every Harmony patch the mod applies maps each one to exactly one switch, none unmapped; pipe-pole switch off: pipe poles change while the power masts' spans, sag and link count read unchanged; captures for the master
leaves.tier_reason: patches and drawing are live
leaves.experience: The player flips the master switch off and sees vanilla conduit and lamp art come back without a restart; flips each feature switch, including keep wires on gravship, cut wires on owner change, drip loops and slide under, and sees just that feature change; the FlowWorks pipe-pole switch moves pipe poles and leaves power poles alone. It must not read as a switch that does nothing, or one that needs a restart.
leaves.scenario: For the master and each feature switch: read the feature's state, flip it, read again, flip back; read lamp art on a styled run under master off and on; list every applied Harmony patch against its switch; pipe-pole switch flipped with GSS master both on and off, power masts read before and after each flip.
false_pass: the setting value changes while the patch stays applied
leaves.red: turning drip loops off leaves drip loops drawn, or the master switch needs a restart

leaves.oracle_proposed: the drawing_true_to_grid read passes on the landed ship; with the switch off its stated behaviour holds
leaves.tier_reason: a gravship launch needs Odyssey's flight and a landing map, more than a quicktest stages reliably; the minimal list with all DLC holds it
leaves.experience: The player flies a gravship with cords aboard and, after it lands, sees cords that still explain the real connections aboard; the exact drawing may change. It must not read as cords left behind, cords to nothing, or no cords at all.
leaves.scenario: A gravship with conduit, a battery and two consumers; launch and land; run the drawing-true-to-grid read on the landed ship; repeat with keep wires on gravship off.
false_pass: the read taken before launch
leaves.red: after landing the ship's devices have no cords, or cords lead off the ship

leaves.oracle_proposed: after the claim: no link between the claimed mast and either mast of ours, the OwnerMismatchSweep cut count equals the cut links, the message shown; the span between two masts of ours that does not touch the claimed mast stays linked and powered; with the switch off the links stay
leaves.tier_reason: factions and anchor links are live state
leaves.experience: The player whose pole is claimed or captured by another faction sees every wire between that pole and a pole of a different owner taken down and coiled, with a message saying so; wires between poles of one owner stay up. It must not read as our power still feeding a pole someone else now owns, or wires that vanish with no sign.
leaves.scenario: Three powered masts of ours in a line, the middle one spanned to both, and a fourth mast of ours spanned to the first; hand the middle mast to another faction; read every link and the power; repeat with cutWiresOnOwnerChange off.
false_pass: the link drops because the faction change itself destroys the anchor, not because the owner sweep cut it
only the setting value is read, never a claimed pole
the sweep cuts every span on the net or on any owner change, so the same-owner span drops too
leaves.red: after a pole changes owner its wire to our pole stays strung and our net still powers it, or wires drop with no message

leaves.oracle_proposed: in game 1 the tap registry lists the tap, the style picks list both runs, the printed-section static set (SectionLayer_RM_MessyCords.PrintedStatic: section keys, strand names) is non-empty and the live-wire path-cost table (RM_LiveWirePathCost) holds this map id; in a new game and in a game reached by loading a tap-free save, at start, all four are empty, and the new game's floor run prints its cords; loading game 1's own save brings its tap, picks, printed sections and priced cells back
leaves.tier_reason: static state across two games exists only in a running session
leaves.experience: The player who quits one game and starts or loads another in the same session sees nothing of the first carried over: no tap from the old game is still registered and draining goodwill, runs take fresh looks rather than the old game's picks, the new game's cords all draw, and pawns walk freely over cells that were live wire only in the old game. It must not read as an old game's theft or styles haunting a new one, cords missing in the new game, or pawns avoiding ground with no wire on it.
leaves.scenario: A quicktest colony with a clamped tap, two styled runs and a live fallen wire, saved; read the tap registry, style picks, printed-section statics and live-wire path costs; start a second quicktest in the same session, lay a floor run, and read them again; then, from the filled first game, load a save that holds no tap, no styled run and no fallen wire and read them again.
false_pass: the read in the second game looks at a fresh instance the mod never fills, so it is empty whether or not the old state was cleared
only a new game tested, so the load path, which initialises differently, keeps the old game's tap
only the tap registry and style picks read, so a stale printed-section key leaves the new game's cords unprinted or game 1's priced cells make new pawns avoid bare ground
leaves.red: a tap from the first game is still in the registry in the second game, or the second game's runs reuse the first game's style picks

leaves.oracle_proposed: offline scan: no ThingDef, texture or class for hoses or reels under src/RimMandrake/GimmeSomeSlack
leaves.experience: The reader of the mod's defs and source finds no hose, reel or pipe drawing in Gimme Some Slack: it draws power cords only, hoses live in FlowWorks. It must not read as a hose def or texture left behind.
leaves.scenario: Scan GSS defs and C# for hose, reel and pipe drawing classes and textures.
